tier_reason: Upgraded C to A: benchmark code is public (benchmarks/bench.cpp, driven as ./build/nexus_bench per docs/build.md), compiler GCC 16.2.1, CPU Intel i7-12650H, and flags are derivable from the public CMakeLists.txt (CMake Release, i.e. -O3 -DNDEBUG, plus -fcontracts -fcontract-evaluation-semantic=ignore, no -march), as with the lzbench Makefile-flags precedent. Numbers are first-party, best of three runs.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README table (8 workers, best of three): fire-and-forget 8.39 M tasks/s vs Taskflow 1.24 and BS::thread_pool 0.40; submit-and-get 2.09 vs 0.38 and 0.27; recursive fork-join 28.40 M leaf tasks/s vs 8.62 and 1.23; 8x multi-producer 7.60 vs 2.76 and 1.36; round-trip P50/P99 0.44/0.87 us vs Taskflow 2.66/7.44 and BS 3.75/6.01. docs/build.md extended run vs oneTBB: fire-and-forget 8.40 vs 3.65, fork-join 27.39 vs 25.69 (about 1.07x, derived from page data), multi-producer 7.31 vs 6.53.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: GCC 16.2.1, C++26, CMake Release (-O3 -DNDEBUG) plus -fcontracts -fcontract-evaluation-semantic=ignore and -Wall -Wextra -Wshadow from CMakeLists.txt; no -march
corrections.caveats: First-party, best of three runs on one laptop CPU (i7-12650H), README and docs in Chinese. A oneTBB comparison does exist in docs/build.md (oneTBB linked only if found at configure time): nexus leads clearly on fire-and-forget but only about 7% on recursive fork-join and 12% on multi-producer. The workloads hit a shared atomic counter, so they mostly measure scheduling overhead; docs/build.md says that on a fixed compute workload at 4 threads nexus takes 3.26 ms vs Taskflow 2.59 ms (slower). Requires GCC 16.2+ with C++26 contracts. Very new project with 1 star.

notes: README numbers match exactly. Record caveat claiming no oneTBB row was wrong; docs/build.md has one. Metadata (MIT, 1 star, not a fork, active) confirmed on the github.com page and the LICENSE file; last commit date taken from the record (benchmark dated 2026-09-30), not re-checked commit by commit.

tier_reason: First-party Google Benchmark output in the README, from the public benchmark/ directory, with GCC 13 and an Apple M1 Pro, but no compiler flags stated, so not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Mixed against std::execution::par (GCC 13, M1 Pro): exclusive_scan 11.6 ms vs 19.8 ms (about 1.7x, derived from page data) vs sequential 33.7 ms; sort 112 ms vs 113 ms (parity), pluggable_sort with pdqsort 71.7 ms; for_each 18.7 vs 15.3 ms, transform 17.4 vs 15.3 ms, reduce 4.06 vs 3.38 ms, find_if at the 5th percentile 0.405 vs 0.230 ms (all slower); all_of 3.47 vs 3.45 ms (parity). About 5x faster than sequential on most algorithms.

notes: Numbers match the README exactly. Its real value is as a dependency-free fallback where native std::execution::par is missing (Apple Clang, Emscripten); against native par it wins only in exclusive_scan and with a pluggable sort. baseline_stdlib set to libstdc++ because GCC 13 ships libstdc++ (whose par backend is TBB), inferred, not stated. Licenses, 38 stars and last commit 2024-06-03 (stale) confirmed on github.com.

tier_reason: A third-party competitor's nanobench comparison (DeveloperPaul123/thread-pool, with public benchmark code) on a Ryzen 7 5800X using Clang and MSVC, but no flags stated and it is not a well-known independent suite, so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Clang results (relative to dp::thread_pool with std::function = 100%): Thiefpool 98.3-99.0% vs BS::thread_pool 90.2-94.5%; 1024x1024: 52.80 ms/op vs BS 57.14 ms/op, about 8% faster (derived from page data); 8x8: 172.33 vs 188.16 ms. MSVC 256x256: 93.18 vs 99.73 ms. task_thread_pool beats Thiefpool at 8x8 to 256x256 (e.g. 154.74 vs 172.33 ms at 8x8).
corrections.caveats: The only published numbers come from another pool's README benchmark (dp::thread_pool). The repo has its own benchmark/bench.cpp (10M enqueue micro-benchmark) but publishes no results. Compiler flags not stated, Windows machine with frequency scaling noted, error margins up to 1.4%. Differences are small: Thiefpool is about 1-2% behind dp::thread_pool and behind task_thread_pool at small and medium sizes, ahead only of BS::thread_pool. BS::thread_pool is not TBB, OpenMP or Rayon. Last commit 2023-03-26, more than 3 years ago.

notes: Clang and MSVC numbers match the dp::thread_pool result pages. Corrected maintenance to abandoned (last commit 2023-03-26 is more than 3 years before 2026-10) and the caveat about the repo having no benchmark. MPL-2.0 and 117 stars confirmed.
